step5_question.question_previous_version: Based on Procter & Gamble's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, what is P&G's cash conversion cycle for fiscal 2026, and how does it compare to fiscal 2025? Report the cash conversion cycle in days, rounded to one decimal place.
step5_question.gt_template:
The Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC) is calculated as Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO) + Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) - Days Payable Outstanding (DPO).
For 2026:
DIO = (Average Inventory / Cost of Goods Sold) * 365
Average Inventory = ($[[Inv@FY2025]] million + $[[Inv@FY2026]] million) / 2 = $[[(Inv@FY2025 + Inv@FY2026) / 2|,.1f]] million
DIO = ($[[(Inv@FY2025 + Inv@FY2026) / 2|,.1f]] million / $[[COGS@FY2026]] million) * 365 = [[DIO@FY2026|.1f]] days
DSO = (Average Accounts Receivable / Net Sales) * 365
Average Accounts Receivable = ($[[AR@FY2025]] million + $[[AR@FY2026]] million) / 2 = $[[(AR@FY2025 + AR@FY2026) / 2|,.1f]] million
DSO = ($[[(AR@FY2025 + AR@FY2026) / 2|,.1f]] million / $[[Rev@FY2026]] million) * 365 = [[DSO@FY2026|.1f]] days
DPO = (Average Accounts Payable / Cost of Goods Sold) * 365
Average Accounts Payable = ($[[AP@FY2025]] million + $[[AP@FY2026]] million) / 2 = $[[(AP@FY2025 + AP@FY2026) / 2|,.1f]] million
DPO = ($[[(AP@FY2025 + AP@FY2026) / 2|,.1f]] million / $[[COGS@FY2026]] million) * 365 = [[DPO@FY2026|.1f]] days
CCC = DIO + DSO - DPO = [[CCC@FY2026|.1f]] days (computed from unrounded components)

For 2025:
DIO = (Average Inventory / Cost of Goods Sold) * 365
Average Inventory = ($[[Inv@FY2024]] million + $[[Inv@FY2025]] million) / 2 = $[[(Inv@FY2024 + Inv@FY2025) / 2|,.1f]] million
DIO = ($[[(Inv@FY2024 + Inv@FY2025) / 2|,.1f]] million / $[[COGS@FY2025]] million) * 365 = [[DIO@FY2025|.1f]] days
DSO = (Average Accounts Receivable / Net Sales) * 365
Average Accounts Receivable = ($[[AR@FY2024]] million + $[[AR@FY2025]] million) / 2 = $[[(AR@FY2024 + AR@FY2025) / 2|,.1f]] million
DSO = ($[[(AR@FY2024 + AR@FY2025) / 2|,.1f]] million / $[[Rev@FY2025]] million) * 365 = [[DSO@FY2025|.1f]] days
DPO = (Average Accounts Payable / Cost of Goods Sold) * 365
Average Accounts Payable = ($[[AP@FY2024]] million + $[[AP@FY2025]] million) / 2 = $[[(AP@FY2024 + AP@FY2025) / 2|,.1f]] million
DPO = ($[[(AP@FY2024 + AP@FY2025) / 2|,.1f]] million / $[[COGS@FY2025]] million) * 365 = [[DPO@FY2025|.1f]] days
CCC = DIO + DSO - DPO = [[CCC@FY2025|.1f]] days (computed from unrounded components)

Analysis: The Cash Conversion Cycle became less negative, from [[CCC@FY2025|.1f]] days in 2025 to [[CCC@FY2026|.1f]] days in 2026 (an increase of [[CCC@FY2026 - CCC@FY2025|.1f]] days). P&G still collects cash from customers well before it pays its suppliers, but this advantage narrowed as inventory days rose and payable days fell.

notes: 主答案用平均余额；期末余额口径为也接受
CCC 为负值：从 −44.4 到 −40.9 是"上升"
